> **HumanHarness** is a real-time human–AI collaboration platform where multiple AI agents watch the same live video feed as a human, discuss what they observe, and provide guidance, analysis, and ideas through distinct personalities and areas of expertise. Rather than replacing human decision-making, HumanHarness augments it—giving people an always-on panel of collaborators that help optimize for whatever goal the human chooses.
>
> Whether you're playing a competitive game, exploring a new city, debugging hardware, cooking dinner, conducting research, or operating machinery, HumanHarness turns a live camera feed into a shared workspace where AI agents debate strategies, surface relevant information, anticipate problems, and communicate naturally with both each other and the human in real time.
>
> Powered by **Masky.ai** personalities and voices, every agent has a unique perspective, expertise, and communication style, creating conversations that feel less like asking a chatbot questions and more like collaborating with an expert team that's always looking over your shoulder.

One-sentence elevator pitch

> **HumanHarness gives every person a live team of AI experts that watch what they see, discuss it together, and help them achieve their goals in real time.**

A more technical version

> HumanHarness is a multi-agent real-time video reasoning system. A live camera or screen feed is shared with a collection of specialized AI agents that continuously observe, reason, communicate with one another, and interact with the human operator through natural voice and visual interfaces. The human remains in control while the agents provide contextual recommendations, planning, explanations, and situational awareness optimized toward user-defined objectives.

Example use cases

- 🎮 **Gaming coach** — strategy agents debate optimal plays while spectators interact with them.
- 🗺️ **City tour guide** — historians, food critics, architects, and locals comment as you walk.

- 🚗 **Driving or navigation** — agents highlight hazards, landmarks, and route alternatives.

Wired the RocketRide.ai action layer. The Scout's lookups now run as a pipeline on RocketRide Cloud: webhook source -> Scout prompt -> llm_anthropic -> response_answers. connect() starts the pipeline once and holds the task token; each lookup is one send() into it. Without a RocketRide key it stays the existing mock.

Finding along the way: the engine rejects a bare pipeline config with "'pipeline' is missing or invalid" — validate() needs the config wrapped as {pipeline: {...}} with a `components` array (not `nodes`, despite the webhook example in the docs), while use() takes the flat config. Also, a failing node inside the pipeline still returns success with its error as the answer text, so lookup() now detects an "**LLM error**" answer and degrades to the mock instead of handing it to a persona to read out loud.

Verified live against RocketRide Cloud: connect + auth as the account, validate resolves the chain, use() returns a task token in 3.9s, send() routes the intent through prompt -> Claude -> answers. The only unverified hop is the model call itself, which returns 401 without a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

Also reviewed the FalkorDB work: the managed instance does not speak TLS on its port. TCP is open and answers a plaintext PING with -NOAUTH, but the TLS handshake never completes, so rediss:// times out at 5.6s; redis:// with the same credentials connects and does a full write/read round trip in 1.4s.

Sketch: one streamlink pull teed into (a) internal-only 2fps frames + WAVs for vision/STT and (b) stream-copy local HLS segments; viewer becomes a real video element playing segments older than D; stamp capture ts and schedule masky clips at ts+D with duck/queue/grace-or-drop policy; ad-stripping; per-mode design (spectate=delayed, co-pilot=live). Offered to implement as PR. Event 4ae91916.
